article.title: IELTS Practice: The City as a Heat Trap
article.content:
On a summer evening, a city street can remain hot long after the countryside has cooled. This difference is known as the urban heat island effect. It occurs because roads, roofs, and concrete walls absorb heat during the day and release it slowly after sunset. Traffic, air conditioning units, and industrial activity add more heat to the surrounding air.

The problem is not merely uncomfortable. Higher night-time temperatures can prevent the body from recovering after a hot day, especially for older people and those with health conditions. Heat can also increase electricity demand as more residents use cooling systems. When power networks are already under pressure, this extra demand may create a cycle in which cooling one building contributes to warming the street outside.

City planners have several tools to reduce the effect. Trees provide shade and cool the air through evaporation from leaves. Pale roofs and reflective surfaces can send more sunlight back into the atmosphere instead of absorbing it. Some cities are testing permeable pavements that allow water to pass through and evaporate later. These methods are most effective when they are planned as connected systems rather than isolated decorations.

Urban heat is therefore both an environmental issue and a design challenge. A cooler city is not created by one park or one painted roof, but by thousands of small decisions about materials, streets, water, and shade.
article.translation:
夏日傍晚，城市街道往往在乡村已经降温后仍然炎热。这种差异被称为城市热岛效应。它的产生是因为道路、屋顶和混凝土墙在白天吸收热量，并在日落后缓慢释放。交通、空调设备和工业活动还会向周围空气增加更多热量。

这个问题不仅仅是让人不舒服。较高的夜间温度会阻碍身体在炎热白天后的恢复，尤其影响老年人和有健康问题的人。高温也会增加电力需求，因为更多居民会使用制冷系统。当电网已经承压时，额外需求可能形成循环：给一栋楼降温，却让室外街道更热。

城市规划者有多种减缓方法。树木提供阴影，并通过叶片蒸发冷却空气。浅色屋顶和反射表面能把更多阳光反射回大气，而不是吸收。部分城市正在试验透水铺装，让水穿过地面并在之后蒸发。这些方法如果作为相互连接的系统规划，而不是孤立装饰，效果最好。

因此，城市高温既是环境问题，也是设计挑战。更凉爽的城市不是由一个公园或一片刷白屋顶创造的，而是由关于材料、街道、水和阴影的成千上万个小决定共同塑造的。
article.source: Original IELTS-style text based on NASA public information

questions.prompt: What causes city streets to stay warm after sunset?
options: Urban materials release stored heat slowly
Countryside areas absorb more traffic pollution
Reflective roofs trap warm air underground
Trees prevent heat from escaping
questions.explanation: 第一段说明道路、屋顶和混凝土白天吸热，晚上缓慢释放。

questions.prompt: Why does the passage mention air conditioning?
options: To show how cooling demand can add to urban heat
To prove that electricity is no longer necessary
To argue that all buildings should use the same system
To explain why rural homes are warmer at night
questions.explanation: 第二段指出空调使用会增加电力需求，并可能让室外更热。

questions.prompt: The word 'permeable' in paragraph 3 means able to:
options: reflect sunlight
let water pass through
produce shade
store electricity
questions.explanation: 文中说透水铺装 allow water to pass through。

questions.prompt: What does the writer suggest about heat-reduction methods?
options: They work best as part of a connected plan
They should focus only on city parks
They are mainly decorative features
They cannot affect night-time temperatures
questions.explanation: 第三段最后说这些方法作为连接系统规划时效果最好。

questions.prompt: Which title best summarizes the passage?
options: Designing Cities That Stay Cooler
Why Rural Areas Need More Pavement
The History of Air Conditioning
How Traffic Improves Urban Comfort
questions.explanation: 文章从热岛成因讲到规划解决方案，核心是城市降温设计。
